title: Capability definitions
description: Shared capability definitions (F2-02, schema-strategy). NON-NORMATIVE machine artifact: the normative source is spec/glossary.md, spec/core/permissions.md and spec/core/core-vs-extension.md. A capability is a named, versioned unit of functionality expressed as a contract independent of any concrete vendor implementation.

capabilityId.description: Namespaced capability contract identifier, for example 'models.system-one', 'interfaces.mcp' or 'workflows.arazzo'. Which capabilities exist in the Core versus an extension is OPEN (decision record §58, open question 'core-vs-extension capabilities'): this schema validates shape only and MUST NOT fix the capability registry contents; existence is F2-07. F1: glossary.md 'Capability'; core/core-vs-extension.md §3.

capabilityRequirement.description: A required capability contract, optionally naming a preferred implementation and alternatives. A concrete implementation MUST NOT be required for conformance. F1: core/requirements.md §2.3, §3.

capability.description: The required capability contract. Same identifier shape as capabilityId. F1: core/requirements.md §2.3.

preferred.description: Optional preferred implementation of the capability contract. A concrete implementation MAY be named only as preferred or alternative and MUST NOT be required for conformance. F1: core/requirements.md §2.3.

alternatives.description: Optional alternative implementations, each of which MUST satisfy the same capability contract. F1: core/requirements.md §2.3.
